subject: zoology_2
question_text: Distinguish between diabetes insipidus and diabetes mellitus.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.52, VSAQ 91. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Diabetes insipidus
steps.why: Without vasopressin the kidney cannot take water back, so plain water is lost and thirst follows.
common_mistakes: Giving glucose in the urine. Insipidus means tasteless: there is no sugar.
steps.memory_tip: Insipidus means tasteless: water, no sugar, no vasopressin.
lines: It is due to hyposecretion of vasopressin.

steps.label: Diabetes mellitus
steps.why: With too little insulin the blood sugar rises so high that the kidney cannot hold it back, and it spills into the urine.
common_mistakes: Blaming vasopressin. Mellitus is an insulin problem.
steps.memory_tip: Mellitus means honey: sugar in the urine, insulin too low.
lines: Diabetes mellitus shows excess urine with
glucose and ketone bodies in it.

lines.text: It is due to hyposecretion of insulin

insider_note: This question is asked more often than any other two-mark question in this chapter. Both are 'diabetes' because both pass much urine — the difference is the hormone, so name vasopressin and insulin.
